brand.name: Wayfarer Coffee
brand.one_line_description: A direct-trade coffee subscription that pays farmers before the harvest, not after.
brand.mission: To make specialty coffee's supply chain fair enough that farmers can plan a year ahead, not just survive one.
brand.vision: In five years, Wayfarer is the brand coffee farmers recommend to each other, not just the one drinkers recommend.
brand.positioning_statement: For people who already care where their coffee comes from, Wayfarer is the subscription that pays farmers upfront, because a fair price shouldn't depend on how well the harvest sells.
brand.differentiation: Farmers are paid in full before the beans ship, not on consignment after retail sales — the risk sits with us, not them.

product.name: Wayfarer Subscription
product.description: A recurring shipment of single-origin coffee, roasted within 72 hours of your delivery window.
key_features: Farmer profile and payment date printed on every bag
Skip, swap, or pause any time from the account page
top_benefits: You know exactly whose harvest you're funding
Fresher coffee than anything on a grocery shelf
No guilt about where your money actually goes
product.proof_points: 94% of partner farms have been paid in full before shipment for three consecutive seasons; verified by an independent co-op auditor.
product.category: Most people currently buy bagged specialty coffee from a grocery store or a local roaster with no visibility into farmer payment terms.

audience.primary_audience: Urban professionals, 28-45, who already spend $15+ on coffee weekly and read ingredient labels out of habit.
audience.demographics: Household income $70k+, city or inner-suburb dwellers, college-educated.
audience.psychographics: Values transparency over brand story; skeptical of vague sustainability claims; will pay a premium if the premium is explained.
pain_points: Suspicious that 'fair trade' labels are marketing, not practice
Tired of coffee going stale before they finish the bag
Wants to support farmers directly but has no way to verify it
audience.desired_outcome: Feeling confident their coffee spend is doing what they think it's doing, without having to research it themselves.
audience.objections: Price point is higher than grocery store coffee; subscription fatigue from other services.
audience.secondary_audience: Independent cafes looking for a wholesale partner with verifiable sourcing claims.

we_are: Willing to say when a harvest was mediocre
Written like one person talking to another
we_are_not: Poetic about 'the journey of the bean'
Vague about pricing or payment terms
tone.example_line: This bag paid Marisol's farm in full, six weeks before a single bean was roasted.

offer.core_offer: First bag free with any subscription plan, cancel anytime.
offer.pricing_packaging: $19/month for 12oz biweekly, $34/month for 12oz weekly; discounts for 3- and 6-month prepay.
offer.urgency_reason: Current lot from Marisol's farm in Huila sells out roughly every 3 weeks.
offer.guarantee: Full refund on your first bag if it's not the best coffee you've had delivered.
offer.post_conversion: Welcome email introduces the current farmer, payment date, and expected next-lot rotation.
